newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Consortium seeks Slovenia mobile phone licence.
newsitem.headline: Consortium seeks Slovenia mobile phone licence.

text.p: Slovenian telephone switchboard maker Iskratel said on Tuesday it would apply for the country's second mobile phone licence in a joint venture with three other partners.

Unlisted Iskratel, 48-percent owned by Germany's Siemens, said it had formed a consortium called GSM in an equal partnership with Slovenian export-import company Interevropa, Finland's Telekom, and Slovenian petrol trader Istrabenz.

"We expect the government will grant another licence for a mobile telephone operator later this year and hope our consortium will get the licence," Iskratel's chief executive Andrej Polenc told Reuters.

Currently only state-owned Mobitel has a licence to operate a mobile telephone system in Slovenia. The government has not yet said if and when it might grant another licence. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
